Feminist Retro Gaming Guide

446 games from the arcade era through PS3/360/Wii and every handheld up to the Vita — researched for great female characters, stories that respect them, and the women who built them. Nothing was cut for imperfection: every game shows exactly which criteria it meets (✓), partly meets (◐), fails (✗), or couldn't be verified (?). ⚠ notes tell you the catch before you commit. ★ = hand-picked for Brandon based on the RobitFarmer Backloggd profile. Visual novels, doujin games, and fan-translated imports now live under the platform they released on, and every 🇯🇵 import links its translation patch. ROM hacks ride along as 🧩 sub-items on the game they modify, next to recommended QoL and retranslation patches for emulated play.

★ Final Fantasy VI

1994 · JRPG · SNES
★ For you: You love FF but have never logged a 2D one — Terra and Celes carry the series' best ensemble story; Pixel Remaster trims the friction.

The 16-bit JRPG with two female leads: Terra's arc rejects the weapon men made of her and redefines her worth through chosen family, while Celes — general, opera diva, suicide survivor — carries the entire ruined-world act. Writer-artist Kaori Tanaka (Soraya Saga) authored fan-favorite backstory, and the ensemble's women talk to each other about hope, power, and motherhood constantly.

⚠ 'Inclusive' partial: themes of otherness (Terra's mixed heritage, Gau, disability-coded Cyan grief arc) are strong but implicit; period localization softened some content. Celes's cliff scene depicts attempted suicide — handled seriously, but worth a content note.

★ Super Metroid

1994 · Action-adventure (Metroidvania) · SNES
★ For you: Atmosphere-first, not punishment-first (your Demon's Souls lane) — the 16-bit template for everything you like about Samus Returns.

Samus Aran is the era's defining female protagonist: the 1986 NES Metroid hid her gender until the ending, upending the assumption that action heroes are men, and Super Metroid gives her the genre's greatest solo adventure — competent, silent, never sexualized during play. One entry covers both games since the feminist story spans them.

⚠ Bechdel fails only because there's almost no dialogue and Samus is the sole human. Gaze 'partial' for the infamous reward endings: NES Metroid undresses Samus down to a bikini for fast clears (and the Justin Bailey password plays in a leotard), and Super Metroid's sub-3-hour ending shows her in a swimsuit — her body framed as a prize for player skill.
FC✓ST✓BT✗MG◐MI✓QP✓IN✗WD✓
👩‍💻 Women who made it
  • Minako Hamano — Co-composer (Super Metroid) · Composed several of Super Metroid's tracks with Kenji Yamamoto (e.g., the haunting Maridia themes); one of Nintendo's longest-serving women composers, later lead composer on Metroid Fusion and Zero Mission.

★ Panel de Pon NEW🇯🇵

1995 · Puzzle · Super Famicom
★ For you: Puzzle-genre royalty with an all-fairy cast (Lip!) — your Balatro/Pocket Dungeon puzzle brain will click instantly; it's on NSO.
🇯🇵 Japan-only in 1995; West got the Yoshi-reskinned Tetris Attack

Nintendo's greatest action puzzler originally starred fairy Lip and an all-girl pantheon of flower, water and moon fairies - then the West got it reskinned as Tetris Attack with Yoshi, erasing the entire female cast because girls'-aesthetic branding was deemed unsellable. Playing the Japanese original is reclaiming a classic localization erasure, and it is on NSO worldwide.

⚠ Characters are light puzzle-game archetypes and the fairy-tale story is minimal - the landmark here is the cast's erasure history, not deep writing.

Centipede

1981 · Fixed shooter (arcade) · Arcade, Atari 2600

Co-created and programmed by Dona Bailey, the only woman programmer in Atari's coin-op division, who deliberately steered its palette and feel away from grim shooter machismo — and it became one of the first arcade hits with a huge female playerbase. Included as this catalog's pre-NES historical anchor for women in game development.

⚠ The three 'no's reflect pure abstraction — there are no characters or story to rate, only a garden and a trackball. Inclusive 'partial': consciously designed to welcome players beyond young men, a piece of feminist design history rather than representation.

Donkey Kong NEW

1981 · Arcade platformer · Arcade, NES

Where the damsel in distress enters video games: Pauline — 'Lady' in the Japanese cabinet — is the medium's first kidnapped woman, the sprite crying HELP that fixed the grammar for four decades (Tropes vs. Women in Video Games opens with her). Mike Mika's 2013 Pauline Edition hack, made overnight so his three-year-old daughter could do the rescuing, finally handed her the hammer — and Nintendo eventually followed, reinventing Pauline as New Donk City's mayor, the voice of 'Jump Up, Super Star!', and co-lead of Donkey Kong Bananza (2025).

⚠ The ✗ on female_characters and misogyny_avoided is the historical point: Pauline exists to be carried off — the founding instance of the trope, which the attached hack reverses. Story is four screens of pantomime (remarkable for 1981, still ✗ by this rubric), with no dialogue to test and nothing inclusive to score. 1981 Nintendo/Ikegami Tsushinki credits leave women_on_team unverifiable.
FC✗ST✗BT✗MG✓MI✗QP✓IN✗WD?

Castlevania

1986 · Action platformer · NES/Famicom Disk System

Earns its place for who built it: Konami newcomer Kinuyo Yamashita composed the entire legendary score ('Vampire Killer' remains one of gaming's most covered themes) while credited under the pseudonym 'James Banana.' A landmark case of a woman authoring a franchise's musical identity and being erased from its credits for decades.

⚠ No women in the game itself beyond monster bosses (Medusa) — this is a 'women behind the code' pick, not a representation pick. Story is arcade-thin.

Metroid NEW

1986 · Action-adventure (the Metroidvania ur-text) · NES, Famicom Disk System

The game that hid a woman inside the armor: finish fast enough and Samus removes her helmet, retroactively turning every assumption about 'him' (the manual's own pronoun) back on the player. With the 'JUSTIN BAILEY' password letting anyone play the reveal forward, Metroid gave console gaming its first great female action hero — and it now hosts Rogue Dawn, the acclaimed fan prequel that adds a second woman to its universe.

⚠ Samus in 1986 is a silhouette with agency, not a written character ('partial'); the story lives in the manual and there is no dialogue at all (story/Bechdel ✗). Male gaze 'partial': the faster you finish, the fewer clothes the ending grants her — leotard, then bikini — the era's strip-for-speed reward. Inclusive 'partial' strictly for the reveal itself: the assumed-male hero was a woman all along. R&D1's part-pseudonymous credits leave women_on_team unverifiable.
FC◐ST✗BT✗MG◐MI✓QP✓IN◐WD?

All-new world, graphics and music — routinely ranked among the best NES hacks ever made.
  • HACK Metroid + Saving — snarfblam's quality-of-life patch replaces the password grind with a real save system, making Samus's 1986 debut far more playable on modern hardware. The gentlest way to meet gaming's first great heroine in her original form.

The Legend of Zelda NEW

1986 · Action-adventure · NES, Famicom Disk System

The ur-damsel text: the girl who names the series spends it as a prize at the bottom of a dungeon, a structure a thousand games then copied. It's here as the host of Kenna Warsinske's Zelda Starring Zelda — the 2013 gender-swap that let the princess do the saving, eleven years before Nintendo's own Echoes of Wisdom — and because its open, secret-riddled overworld is still genuinely great to play.

⚠ Rated honestly as the founding case: Zelda is an endpoint rather than a character, Impa exists only in the manual, and the cave women sell potions — female_characters and misogyny_avoided get ✗ because 'save the princess' IS the game, which is precisely what the attached hack answers. No story or dialogue beyond that premise (story/Bechdel/inclusive ✗). Pseudonymous 1986 credits ('S. Miyahon', 'Ten Ten') leave women_on_team unverifiable.
FC✗ST✗BT✗MG✓MI✗QP✓IN✗WD?

Mega Man

1987 · Action platformer · NES

Another foundational score by a woman: Manami Matsumae composed and programmed the sound for the first Mega Man (as 'Chanchacorin'), setting the melodic template for the most beloved soundtrack series on the NES. She's still composing today (Shovel Knight, Mega Man 11 contributions).

⚠ Composer showcase, not a representation pick: Roll exists only as a background 'housekeeping robot' sister — a period-typical gendered role worth naming.

Phantasy Star

1987 · JRPG · Sega Master System

Alis Landale is console RPG's first great female lead — a teenage revolutionary who avenges her brother and topples a tyrant, two years before most JRPGs let women do anything but heal. Co-created by Rieko Kodama ('First Lady of RPGs'), who drew its characters, monsters, and dungeons.

⚠ Bechdel 'partial': Alis speaks with named women (e.g., the healer Suelo), but the sparse script keeps exchanges brief and often brother-adjacent. 'Inclusive' partial for its sci-fi personhood themes (Myau, Noah) rather than explicit representation.

Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom NEW🇯🇵

1988 · Adventure · Famicom, NES (1991, official EN)
🇯🇵 FC 1988; official NES EN localization 1991

Hudson's gentle vegetable-kingdom adventure got an official NES release and remains one of the few nonviolent, menu-driven story games Western NES kids could own. Included with eyes open: you play Sir Cucumber rescuing the captured princess, so it's a damsel plot - but a kind, funny, bloodless one with a memorably resourceful female co-star in Princess Tomato herself.

⚠ Structural damsel-in-distress plot (misogyny 'partial'): the princess is the goal, though she aids the resistance rather than waiting inertly; female cast members rarely speak to each other.

The Guardian Legend

1988 · Shooter / action-adventure hybrid · NES

Compile's cult hybrid stars a lone female cyborg (Miria in Japan) who transforms between starfighter and humanoid to gut an alien world-ship — a woman as pure competent action lead in 1988, with no rescue plot and no male characters at all. Mother (EarthBound Beginnings) NEW🇯🇵

1989 · JRPG · Famicom
🇯🇵 JP 1989; the shelved 1990 'Earth Bound' localization was officially released in 2015 as EarthBound Beginnings

The origin of the Mother series' tender suburban strain of JRPG. Psychic runaway Ana is the party's strongest PSI user, and the whole quest resolves not with a boss kill but with Queen Maria's lullaby — a story that runs on maternal love and remembered song. Japan-only on consoles until Nintendo finally shipped its finished English localization in 2015.

⚠ female_characters: Ana and Queen Maria genuinely matter, but both orbit Ninten's journey and Ana is lightly love-interest-coded. inclusive: nothing notable beyond the mother-centered heart. Brutal early-game difficulty; use the EN release's built-in easy modern conveniences or savestates.

Sweet Home

1989 · Survival-horror RPG · Famicom

The Famicom horror-RPG that begat Resident Evil: three of the five playable film-crew members are women (Akiko, Asuka, Emi), each defined by a skill, not a gender role, and the antagonist Lady Mamiya is a grief-mad mother written with genuine tragedy rather than hag misogyny. Junko Tamiya's score is a masterpiece of Famicom dread.

⚠ Bechdel 'unknown': party dialogue is sparse and utility-driven, so a qualifying woman-to-woman exchange is hard to verify. Japan-only — needs the fan translation.

Super Mario World NEW

1990 · Platformer · SNES

The princess-rescue loop at its most perfected and most invisible: the SNES flagship opens with Peach already taken and closes with the thank-you kiss, the damsel structure so naturalized it reads as landscape. It hosts Peach's Adventure, the 2021 fan campaign that runs the loop in reverse — Bowser kidnaps Mario and Peach goes to war — a flip Nintendo itself only gestured at with Super Princess Peach (2006) and Princess Peach: Showtime! (2024).

⚠ An all-time masterpiece of level design, rated honestly: Peach appears only as premise and prize (female_characters/misogyny_avoided ✗) — the exact loop the attached hack inverts. No story, dialogue between women, or inclusion to score beyond that. Credited staff include no verifiable women ('unknown').

The game that invented the otome genre — made by Koei's Ruby Party, a women-led studio championed by Koei co-founder Keiko Erikawa, who bet (correctly, against the whole industry) that games for women would matter. ⚠ The heroines appear as cute mascot versions with thin in-game writing, and there is barely a story - the feminist interest is the all-shoujo cast and its women creators, not the script.

Tales of Phantasia (and the DeJap fan translation)

1995 · JRPG (fan-translation case study) · Super Famicom

Included as a documented case study in fan-translation misogyny: the famous 2001 DeJap SNES patch inserted crude sexual jokes about party member Arche Klein that do not exist in the Japanese script - a reminder that translation is authorship and that 2000s ROM-hacking culture had a leering streak. Arche herself - a brash half-elf pilot whose arc confronts anti-elf racism - deserved better; the official GBA translation and the Absolute Zero PS1 fan patch provide it.

⚠ The game itself: Arche is lively but the party's women skew archetypal (Mint is a saintly healer), and a hot-spring peeping scene is played for laughs - partial across the board. The DeJap patch specifically scores 'no' on misogyny: its invented Arche vulgarity is the point of this entry. Story is genre-standard. Inomata did not design this entry; the verified woman credit is Arche's PS1 voice actress.

SaGa Frontier

1997 · JRPG (free-scenario) · PS1

Asellus's route is a landmark of queer games history: a girl revived with mystic blood, desired by and drawn to women, choosing between human, half-mystic, and mystic selves - widely read as a coming-out allegory. ⚠ Free-scenario structure leaves every route fragmentary - Asellus's was visibly cut in 1997 and the 1998 localization softened its sapphic text (the 2021 Remaster restores cut events). Emelia's disguises include a bunny suit; occasional cheesecake elsewhere.

The Japanese version is a transhumanist epic — 52 missions, five branching endings, Production I.G cutscenes — that Namco gutted into a plotless 36-mission shooter for the West. It's the pivot the whole series turns on, remade officially as Metroid: Samus Returns (3DS, 2017) and by fans as AM2R, both descended from this strange, claustrophobic Game Boy original.

⚠ Samus's characterization is one wordless act of mercy — the most important act in the series, but still one act (character/story 'partial'; Bechdel ✗ for lack of any dialogue). Male gaze 'partial': the sub-3-hour ending once again undresses her as a speed reward. Inclusive 'partial' for the maternal arc feminist critics have written about ever since. Credits' women unverifiable.

Mother 3

2006 · JRPG · Game Boy Advance

Itoi's anti-capitalist tragedy features Kumatora, a foul-mouthed tomboy princess who is the party's PSI powerhouse and nobody's love interest, and the Magypsies, gender-nonconforming guardians of the world's Needles who mentor the heroes. It is one of the most emotionally serious games on the platform — and one of the most argued-over pieces of queer-adjacent rep of its era.

⚠ Two honest readings of the Magypsies coexist: many queer players cherish them as heroic, joyful, indispensable elders; critics point out they are built on Japan's okama caricature (beard-and-lipstick gags, mincing speech), and localization choices remain debated — both are true, which is why queerphobia/inclusive sit at 'partial'. Misogyny: Hinawa, the mother, dies in chapter 1 as the plot's engine — a fridging by structure, though her grief is honored with unusual seriousness and she recurs meaningfully. Bechdel: named women rarely share scenes; unverified either way.

★ For you: The most beloved feminist/queer-read VN ever made — your Hundred Line 5★ and NitW 5★ both point straight at this gothic ensemble tragedy.

A centuries-spanning gothic tragedy in which a cursed mansion replays era after era of doomed lives — and nearly every era turns out to be an autopsy of gendered violence: witch-hunting, bought brides, women blamed for men's rage — before the frame story flips everything you assumed. Its protagonist Michel is a trans man whose persecution, self-acceptance and love story with Giselle are handled with a seriousness almost unheard of in 2012, and the wronged 'witch' Morgana is allowed her full fury before her peace. Widely regarded as THE feminist/queer-embraced visual novel — routinely at or near the top of VNDB's all-time rankings — and the single most essential VN addition to this catalog.

⚠ ⚠ Depicts sexual violence, torture, domestic abuse and virulent transphobia — always framed as atrocity to be answered, never flavor, but the middle stretch (Doors 3–4) is grueling. Note: writer-director Keika Hanada is often assumed to be a woman but uses he/him in interviews; artist Moyataro's identity is private, so no women-credit is claimed despite the game's reputation.

A quiet historical stepping stone toward the character-driven VNs this catalog is full of.

⚠ ⚠ 18+ eroge framing throughout: every heroine's arc terminates in sex scenes for a male protagonist ('no' on male gaze), Yuka's sexual-exploitation storyline is sympathetic but still sits inside porn structure, and there's an adoptive-sister romance route. Heroines are written with unusual care for 2001 — that's the 'partial', not a pass.

⚠ ⚠ The wider Sono Hanabira franchise this spins off from is explicit 18+ yuri partly aimed at male otaku, with dubious-consent tropes in earlier entries — this entry is the clean standalone one. Story is a slight, cozy slice-of-life ('partial'). Brand staff (writer/artist) are pseudonymous.

Angels of Death (Satsuriku no Tenshi) NEW🇯🇵

2015 · Horror adventure (RPG Maker) · PC
🇯🇵 JP freeware serial 2015–2016; official EN 2016 (Playism)

Rachel 'Ray' Gardner, 13, wakes in the basement of a tower of serial killers and strikes a pact with scythe-swinging Zack: he'll kill her once they escape. Makoto Sanada's doujin megahit (2.7M+ copies, anime adaptation) rides on Ray — flat-voiced, devout, catastrophically damaged — one of doujin horror's most complicated girl protagonists, whose arc is about clawing back a reason to live. Same creator as The Forest of Drizzling Rain (2013), a gentler female-led ghost story also now on Steam.

⚠ ⚠ The central dynamic is a mutual death-pact between an adult killer and a 13-year-old girl — the game knows how wrong that is, but know going in; child abuse backstory, gore, religious mania. Small cast means the only other prominent woman is a sadistic warden (Bechdel 'partial'). Sanada's identity/gender is kept private.

Hello Charlotte (EP1–EP3) NEW

2015 · Adventure trilogy (RPG Maker) · PC

etherane's trilogy starts as candy-colored absurdist horror — puppet-girl Charlotte, her Puppeteer (you), a house of parasites and TV gods — then EP3: Childhood's End detonates it into one of the scene's rawest stories about bullying, psychosis, poverty and fiction as a survival organ. Charlotte's girlhood is revealed as armor someone else built for her; the trilogy interrogates who gets to author a girl's story, including the player.

⚠ ⚠ Self-harm, suicide, vicious bullying, abuse and psychiatric-ward horror, especially in EP3. Creator etherane keeps their identity private, so no women-credit is claimed despite frequent assumption.

Ladykiller in a Bind NEW

2016 · Erotic romance visual novel (ADULTS ONLY) · PC

Christine Love's IGF-winning 'My Twin Brother Made Me Crossdress As Him...': a lesbian jock spends a week impersonating her twin on a schemer-filled cruise, negotiating explicit BDSM encounters where the actual game mechanics are consent, power exchange and social performance. Almost uniquely in erotic games, sex is conversation — who tops, who's performing, who's safe — written from a queer woman's perspective; won Excellence in Narrative at IGF 2017.

⚠ ⚠ Explicit pornography (deliberate, queer-authored — but 'partial' on gaze by definition); at launch it contained a coercive sexual scene that drew heavy criticism, and Love removed it in a 2017 update. Blackmail-driven premise sits deliberately on the consent line elsewhere; adults only.

OneShot NEW

2016 · Meta puzzle adventure · PC

You — literally you, addressed by name through your OS — must guide Niko, a cat-eyed child who uses they/them, across a dying world carrying its replacement sun. Majority-women-made (Casey Gu: art, music, co-writing; Eliza Velasquez: programming, scenario, music), it's the tender end of meta-game design: the fourth-wall tricks exist to make you responsible for one small person, not to smirk at you. Honest note: if quirky meta-games grate on you, this is still that genre — but it's the sincere, bedtime-story version, and Niko's canonical nonbinary pronouns are simply normal in-world.

⚠ Tiny cast with few named women (its heart is a nonbinary child, hence 'partial'/'no' on those axes); meta contrivances (file-system puzzles, talking to you by name) are the whole design — skip if that's a dealbreaker.

Pocket Mirror NEW

2016 · Horror adventure (RPG Maker) · PC

AstralShift's ornate fairytale nightmare: a girl with no name wanders a candlelit dream collecting the shards of herself — Goldia, Fleta, Harpae and Lisette are literally facets of one dissociating psyche, making this a game ABOUT girlhood fractured by trauma, dressed in rococo lace. Made by a Portugal-based team of ~15 with women in core creative roles (lead writer Patrícia 'Ebee' Silva); the studio's sapphic follow-up Little Goody Two Shoes (2023) earned a GLAAD Award nomination.

🔭 Watchlist: no English patch yet 11 games worth knowing about

Japan-only games that would belong in this catalog the day a translation lands. Statuses checked July 2026 — translation projects move fast, so peek at romhacking.net occasionally.

GamePlatformYearWhy it belongs hereStatus
Tokimeki Memorial Girl's Side 4th HeartNintendo Switch2021The only Girl's Side with no way into English — the series is the otome ur-text, built heroine-first (the catalog already has 1st Love Plus), and 4th Heart is its long-awaited modern revival.Active fan TL (meitantei_mae's team, GBAtemp): full script translated and in proofreading as of Feb 2026, no patch released; same group is porting the finished GS1/GS2 DS patches to the Switch remasters.
Twilight Syndrome: Tansaku-hen / Kyuumei-henPS11996Human's schoolgirl-horror duology — Yukari, Chisato and Mika investigate urban legends by flashlight — is the girl-led foundation stone of Japanese horror games (Fatal Frame's lineage), written with real teen-girl interiority.Fan translations of the Syndrome trilogy (including Suda51's Moonlight Syndrome) in progress via the Paradise Hotel 51 circle, public updates through 2025; nothing released as of mid-2026.
Harukanaru Toki no Naka de 3: IzayoikiPS2 (PSP/DS ports)2004Ruby Party's best-regarded Neoromance epic: priestess Nozomi time-loops through the Genpei War and can rewrite it herself — the acclaimed sequel line to the catalog's Harukanaru pick, all still Japan-only.No official EN ever (only the anime was licensed); a solo script-extraction attempt at Haruka 4 stalled in 2023; no active project for any entry.
Angelique LuminariseNintendo Switch2021Koei's women-led Ruby Party rebooting the first otome series ever (the catalog covers the 1994 original) for its 25th anniversary — still no Angelique game has ever been localized.No patch project known; only fan-blog translations of character profiles and short stories (Illusionary Theatre).
Princess Maker 4PS2 / PSP / DS / PC2005The missing mainline entry in the daughter-raising series the catalog covers via Princess Maker 2 — the only numbered PM never released in English while 1, 2, 3 and 5 all reached Steam officially.Partial menu/status patches only (PC and an abandoned DS v0.1); no full translation project known.
Boku no Natsuyasumi 3 & 4PS3 / PSP2007Millennium Kitchen's summer-vacation diaries are quiet domestic storytelling where aunts, mothers and girl cousins carry their own arcs — rare games about family life observed from a child's eye.No project for 3 or 4; Hilltop Works' complete patches for Boku no Natsuyasumi Portable (2022) and BokuNatsu 2 (Nov 2023) proved the demand, so hopes are high.
Tokyo Majin Gakuen KenpuchoPS1 (PSP rereleases)1998Shibuya occult VN/SRPG hybrid whose co-ed devil-hunter class treats its women (Komaki, Aoi, Sakurako and more) as full combat leads and POV characters — a formative urban-fantasy ensemble years before Persona 3.No translation project known for the PS1 original or its PSP rereleases; only the 2007 anime adaptation made it West.
Tantei Jinguji Saburo classic seriesPS11996Data East's hardboiled Shinjuku detective series is co-anchored by investigator Yoko Misono, one of Japanese adventure gaming's longest-serving working women — decades of cases the West only glimpsed via DS-era 'Jake Hunter'.No fan projects for the PS1 entries (Mikan no Rupo, Yume no Owari ni, etc.); only Jake Hunter DS (2008) and Daedalus (2019) got official EN.
Ore no Shikabane o Koete YukePS1 (PSP remaster 2011)1999Sony's generational clan-RPG where short-lived heroes — women as often as men — pass the family's fate down through bloodlines; its Vita sequel Oreshika: Tainted Bloodlines got an official EN release in 2015 and belongs in the main catalog.PSP-version fan TL abandoned in 2018 at under 2%; revived by a new hacker in Aug 2024 (tools/scripts on GitHub); no patch released.
Sakura Taisen GB2: Thunderbolt SakusenGame Boy Color2001The second portable Flower Division adventure, continuing the catalog's Sakura Wars thread with the all-women steam-fighter troupe in trainee-scale form.No project known for GB2; the first Sakura Wars GB already has a complete fan patch ('Go Forth, Young Cadet!'), so GB2 is the remaining gap.
Baroque SyndromePS12000Sting's visual-novel prequel to cult roguelike Baroque, whose apocalypse mythology pivots on female divinity and consuming grief — the last untranslated piece of the Baroque lore now that the mainline versions are patched.No project known; mainline Baroque (Saturn and PS1) both received complete fan patches in July 2023 (Plissken), leaving only this prequel VN.

How ratings work. Every rating is a judgment call from published criticism, fan discussion (ResetEra, Backloggd lists, Tumblr, video essays), credits databases (MobyGames, VGMdb, Wikipedia) and — where possible — primary staff interviews. "Partial" means mixed: worth playing with eyes open. Bechdel = two named women speak to each other about something other than a man; it's a floor, not a medal. Women's credits were individually verified where marked; "unknown" means credits research came up short, not that no women worked on it — game credits before ~2000 are notoriously incomplete and often hid women behind pseudonyms.

Playing today. NSO = Nintendo Switch Online retro libraries (NES/SNES/GB/GBA/N64/GC). Emulator names are the community standards (snes9x, DuckStation, PCSX2, Dolphin, PPSSPP, melonDS, Citra, Vita3K, RPCS3). Fan translations and ROM hacks live at romhacking.net — patches are legal; sourcing ROMs is your call. Built July 2026 for Brandon's Feminist Gaming project.
